newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds see-saw higher in line with Treasuries.
newsitem.headline: Bunds see-saw higher in line with Treasuries.

text.p: Bund futures were slightly higher in late trade, spending a second day more closely following U.S. economic fundamentals than events closer to home.
The December DTB Bund future was up six basis points to 99.59 in late trade, nearly in the middle of the day's range of 99.51 to 99.84.

Bunds were lifted to near their highs for the day after U.S. third quarter GDP showed a 2.2 percent increase, but gave back much of those gains after U.S. home sales figures showed their second highest level since April 1986.
The short end of the German yield curve underperfomred after the interest rate hike in the London raised concerns that the German interest rate cycle may have bottomed out.
The T-note/Bund spread narrowed to 46 basis points from 55 basis points after the release of U.S. third quarter GDP.

Bundesbank chief economist Otmar Issing kept the German central bank in the headlines, telling a German magazine that he saw no need for a rate cut at the moment, but that he would review the situation if events changed.
But such comments are looking especially tired in view of constant Bundesbank jawboning about interest rates.
"It is hard to understand if the Bundesbank is intentionally trying to keep the market off balance, or if we are just seeing council members speaking their own minds," one bond market analyst said.
Now that U.S. GDP is out of the way, the market is turning its focus to American unemployment figures which are due on Friday and may well reveal if the Federal Reserve needs to lift interest rates.
Even if the jobs data comes in on the weak side, some analysts doubt the contract can climb above 100 given the narrowing spread between Bunds and Treasuries.
